text/plain.example:
Common Shade: for AI agents
Updated 2026-11-13. Human edition: https://beattheheat.asia/

A free, open, non-commercial evidence base on extreme heat in South and Southeast Asia: how heat harms health, income and homes, how one harm leads to the next, what helps, and who could act and who could pay. Every claim links to its source and says how sure the evidence is.

status: beta | cost: free | account required: no | coverage: South Asia and Southeast Asia | language: en

text/plain.example:
# Common Shade

> An interactive systems map of extreme heat in Asia: how heat ripples through 10 systems and 90 consequences, the 21 vicious cycles that make it worse, the 33 actions that could break them, and the 14 kinds of institution that hold those levers. Every claim links to its source.

Common Shade's beta platform is at beattheheat.asia and is moving to commonshade.asia; it was first published as BeatTheHeat.Asia. It is independent of the Beat the Heat initiative that UNEP's Cool Coalition runs with the COP30 Presidency.

example.text: Every fraction of a degree avoided weakens every loop that runs through land, ice and forests at once. It also keeps more places within the limits to adaptation, where protecting people still works.
example.example: Across 2.7 million firms in 23 advanced economies, places used to heat coped better with days of 30–35 °C, but none had adapted to days above 40 °C. Each degree avoided keeps more days below that line.

example.peak: Coastal Odisha, not known for extreme heat
example.toll: 2,042 deaths from heatstroke recorded by hospitals
example.what: Heat struck a coastal state with little past experience of extreme heat, and hospitals counted more than two thousand heatstroke deaths in a single month.
